HOW TO READ THIS CONCEPTUAL MODEL
1. Rectangles: entities with business attributes. Diamonds: relationships. No SQL types or foreign keys.
2. [ID]: conceptual identity. [unique]: alternate identifier. ?: optional attribute. Composite identities use +.
3. Multiplicity near an entity counts its instances for ONE instance at the opposite end; N means many.
4. Customer and Supplier are optional, overlapping User profiles. A user may have both profiles and several roles.
5. Reservation items refer to physical units from one supplier. startDate and returnDate are both inclusive.
6. Tool images and physical units are independent sets. Availability and totals are derived, not stored attributes.
7. Minimum 1 item applies to a reservation with selected units and to an issued invoice.
8. UnitDelivery is identified by its ReservationItem; UnitReturn by its delivery. The original composite identity is
9. Critical extensions preserve session, policy, termination, delivery, extension and refund history.
Seven independent facts added in 4NF; lines show ownership or settlement and endpoint labels show multiplicity.
Security facts are independent multivalued sets per User. Policies and rates are versioned; Reservation stores the applied identity and monetary snapshot.
